headline: SILVER CRASHES 9%, GOLD TUMBLES 2% AS U.S. INFLATION DATA FANS FED RATE-HIKE FEARS
snippet: Gold fell 1.83% to $4,564/oz and silver crashed 10.61% on Friday as April CPI came in at 3.8% — the highest reading since May 2023 — driving money markets to price in a 50% chance of a December Fed rate hike. The gold/silver ratio widened sharply to 58.9:1 as silver bore the brunt of the inflation shock.

headline: EQUINOX GOLD SWALLOWS ORLA MINING IN $18.5B DEAL — CANADA'S NEW SENIOR GOLD PRODUCER
snippet: Equinox Gold agreed to acquire Orla Mining in a mostly-stock deal creating a combined $18.5 billion entity with projected annual production of 1.1 million oz — Canada's second-largest gold producer. Shareholders vote in July; deal closes Q3 2026. Orla holders receive one Equinox share plus $0.0001 cash per share.

headline: INDIA DOUBLES GOLD AND SILVER IMPORT DUTIES TO 15% TO DEFEND RUPEE
snippet: India raised gold and silver import tariffs from 6% to 15% — a 10% basic customs duty plus 5% infrastructure levy — to protect the rupee against West Asia conflict pressures. Analysts warn the move will dampen demand in the world's second-largest gold market, while industry officials caution that higher duties could revive bullion smuggling.

headline: COPPER EXTENDS RETREAT AS STRONGER DOLLAR AND HOT U.S. INFLATION DATA BITE
snippet: Copper futures dropped to ~$6.30/lb on May 15 for a second straight session of losses as accelerating U.S. CPI data reinforced rate-hike expectations and a surging dollar made the metal more expensive for Chinese buyers. Goldman Sachs expects a refined copper tariff of at least 25% from Washington shortly after June, adding further supply-chain uncertainty.

headline: NEXGEN Q1 2026: ROOK I BREAKS GROUND THIS SUMMER — COULD SUPPLY 20% OF WORLD URANIUM
snippet: NexGen Energy's Q1 2026 earnings call confirmed construction of the Rook I uranium mine in northern Saskatchewan begins summer 2026, following March CNSC approval. At full capacity, Rook I could produce ~30 million lbs U3O8 annually — roughly 20% of current global uranium supply and over 50% of Western supply — with a four-year build schedule and 700 permanent jobs at steady state.

headline: FORGET MP MATERIALS: THESE TWO RARE EARTH STOCKS SURGE AS CHINA TIGHTENS ITS GRIP
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) is up 274% with $354M in Pentagon contracts and a Texas magnet plant under construction; Critical Metals (CRML) controls 92.5% of Greenland's Tanbreez deposit — the largest rare earth resource outside China — containing all eight key heavy REEs including dysprosium and terbium. Both are surging as China tightens export controls on critical minerals amid the ongoing trade war.

headline: SILVER PRICE OUTLOOK MAY 2026: STOP CHASING THE NUMBER
snippet: GoldSilver.com argues that retail investors piling into silver after its 134% year-over-year run are misreading the metal's dual monetary-industrial identity — and that Friday's 9% crash is precisely what happens when momentum crowds get caught on the wrong side of an inflation shock. The piece outlines a structured accumulation thesis rather than a reactive chase of short-term price action.

headline: GOLD AT $5,000? INSTITUTIONAL FORECASTERS SAY YES — HERE'S WHY THE THESIS SURVIVES
snippet: Despite gold's worst week in months, JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs maintain $5,000/oz targets, pointing to central bank buying still running above 1,000 tonnes annually, geopolitical risk from West Asia, and structural underallocation in gold ETFs as durable tailwinds. The current selloff is framed as a tactical pullback driven by rate-hike fears, not a reversal of the secular bull market.

headline: GDX UP 108% YEAR-OVER-YEAR — GOLD MINERS ARE FINALLY OUTRUNNING THE METAL ITSELF
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF has returned 108% over the past year — more than 80 percentage points ahead of the S&P 500 — as operational leverage converts gold price gains into free cash flow without proportional cost increases. Analysts identify a potential third buy cycle forming in 2026 even after Friday's pullback, noting miners remain broadly undervalued relative to the gold price.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE NEARLY DOUBLES IN Q1 2026 AS SURPLUS-TO-DEFICIT DEBATE HEATS UP
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate surged from $8,259 to $26,278/t in Q1 2026 as the market pivots toward a potential structural deficit — though analysts remain sharply divided, with Wood Mackenzie projecting a continued surplus and Morgan Stanley forecasting an 80,000 mt deficit. Global EV sales tracking above 25 million units annually is the underlying demand driver underpinning the recovery.
